subject: Recap + next steps: PHI handling, BAA availability & eligible deployment modes
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Schultz <dana.schultz@cardiohealth.io>, Alex Rios <alex.rios@cardiohealth.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: PHI handling, BAA availability & eligible deployment modes

Hi Dana / Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Key points from our discussion:
- SOC 2: Redwood has SOC 2 in flight (Type II) — target completion Q1 2027. We can share interim controls documentation in the meantime.
- BAA availability: We can sign a BAA for Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Hosted (multi-tenant) can be scoped for PHI only under an enterprise agreement that includes customer-managed keying and private tenancy; that path requires legal review.
- PHI handling boundaries: Redwood’s recommended pattern is to avoid persistent PHI storage in hosted unless the customer manages the keys. For Dedicated/Private we can support request-level processing with configurable retention policies and audit logs. Please share any special data residency requirements.
- Eligible deployment modes (summary):
  * Private (on-prem / air-gapped) — full PHI support, customer controls KMS, supports regulatory controls.
  * Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) — supports PHI with KMS integration + strict network controls; requires contract addendum.
  * Hosted API (standard) — not recommended for PHI unless enterprise-level contract with BYOK and tenancy isolation is in place.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Please complete the attached vendor security questionnaire (CardioHealth_vendor_survey.xlsx) and return by next Wed (10/7).
2) Share a simple data-flow diagram (PNG or PDF) showing where PHI originates and which downstream systems receive it.
3) Security deep-dive: propose Thurs 10/8 10:00–11:00 PT — please confirm a time that works for your security team.

I’ve attached a short deployment matrix summary (we’ll update with the SOC 2 report once available). Marissa / Karthik — looping you both for any technical clarifications and to pick up the questionnaire review.

Best,
Jonas
-----
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: CardioHealth Security <security@cardiohealth.io>

Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: PHI handling, BAA availability & eligible deployment modes

Thanks Jonas — useful recap. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we kick off the questionnaire: 

1) BAA scope: CardioHealth needs confirmation that a BAA covers any service path that ingests PHI (even transiently). Is Redwood able to commit to BAA coverage for Dedicated and Private, and provide the standard BAA template for our legal team to review?

2) SOC 2 Type II: you mentioned Q1 2027 target — can you provide an expected delivery date for the full Type II report or an interim bridge letter? Our procurement requires evidence of SOC 2 controls for vendors handling PHI.

3) KMS / key custody: for Dedicated deployments, can the customer retain key ownership (BYOK) via cloud KMS/HSM? We need a clear statement of whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys for the model serving path and for any persisted artifacts (logs, caches).

4) Questionnaire timeline: we’ll prioritize the survey once we get the high-level answers above and a draft BAA. Also attaching a short appendix with our compliance baseline and a handful of extra questions to fold into the vendor survey.

Proposed times for a security deep-dive next week: Thu 10/8 09:00–10:00 PT or Fri 10/9 11:00–12:00 PT. Please confirm.

Regards,
CardioHealth Security
security@cardiohealth.io
Attachment: CardioHealth_Security_Appendix.pdf (PDF)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: CardioHealth Security <security@cardiohealth.io>, Dana Schultz <dana.schultz@cardiohealth.io>, Alex Rios <alex.rios@cardiohealth.io>

Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 15:45:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: PHI handling, BAA availability & eligible deployment modes

Hi — thanks for the questions. Below are direct answers and pointers to docs we can share ahead of the deep-dive.

1) BAA scope: Confirmed — Redwood will sign a BAA that covers processing of PHI for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted multi-tenant we can offer a BAA under an enterprise contract that includes additional tenancy/isolation and BYOK; that requires legal review and an addendum. I’ll ask legal to push a draft BAA to you by 10/6.

2) SOC 2 Type II: Our Type II audit is scheduled to complete 2027-02-15. We can provide a SOC 2 Type I report, our control matrix, and an interim attestation letter from our security group in the next week.

3) KMS / key custody:
- Dedicated: supports customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers and HSM integration for encryption at-rest for persisted artifacts (models, caches). Keys can be rotated per customer policy.
- Private (on-prem): customer retains full control over KMS/HSM.
- Hosted: BYOK is available for enterprise customers via dedicated tenancy path only; standard hosted does not expose customer KMS.

4) Questionnaire and next steps: attached is a quick deployment matrix CSV with the high-level answers (redwood_deployment_matrix.csv). Please complete the vendor survey; we’ll have Marissa/Karthik review your responses and follow up with any technical evidence. 

Deep-dive availability: Thu 10/8 09:00–10:00 PT works for our security + infra folks. Please send calendar invite with dial-in.
